protocol.description:
The kv_store protocol is implemented for a key-value store for applications.
App-scoped and tavern-scoped values may hold secrets. By default, their goal isolation is from sandboxed applications, not unrestricted processes running as the same user. Unbounded values are shared and must not hold secrets.
Values are persisted in plaintext. The store has no password or lock/unlock state, and initialization must not depend on a display or user interaction. Encryption at rest, if desired, is provided externally, for example by disk encryption. Filesystem and sandbox isolation must prevent sandboxed applications from accessing the backing files directly; protocol namespace checks still apply. Alternative implementations might provide file-backed encryption (e.g. like KWallet for D-Bus) but it is not a requirement.
kv_store is an exclusive protocol. It must be exposed with the exclusivity flag. Its provider must be the KV barmaid started and authenticated by the tavern. The tavern reserves this protocol name for that provider; exclusivity or a provider-supplied name alone does not authenticate a secret store.
For routed connections, the provider must redeem the connection principal token before serving values. App namespaces use the pair of tavern-attested identity kind and application identifier, never a caller-supplied name, PID, sandbox-local executable path, or routed socket peer credentials. App-scoped operations fail with identity_unavailable without a stable attested identity.
Tavern-scoped values require the tavern's authenticated internal authority; ordinary permission bypass does not grant access. These identity and authority checks use the admitted principal, not later grant changes.

value.name: tavern_value
value.description: Restricted to clients with the core.unobtainium.tavernkeep permission

value.name: identity_unavailable
value.description: App-scoped storage requires a stable attested identity

value.name: permission_denied
value.description: The admitted principal cannot access this value type

object.name: hp_hyprtavern_kv_store_manager_v1
object.description:
This object is a core manager object bound upon creation.
At most one get_value or set_value request for a given (key, type) pair may be pending on this object. Wait for value_obtained, value_stored, or value_failed before requesting the same pair again; other pairs may be used concurrently. A duplicate pending request is a protocol error.

c2s.name: set_value
c2s.description:
Set a value in the kv store.
An app value is restricted to the stable tavern-attested application identity associated with this connection. Executable paths within different sandboxes do not define a shared application namespace.
An unbounded value is a value in a global value pool. It is highly recommended to use unique prefixes e.g. myapp:value to avoid trampling other values. Prefixes are a naming convention, not an access restriction: any admitted client may read or overwrite unbounded values.
It is recommended to prefer app values unless an unbounded one is necessary.
The key must be nonempty and contain only ASCII letters, numbers, or any of the characters: `:/.,-+=?`, otherwise an invalid_key_name error is raised. Values are NUL-free strings; applications must encode binary data, for example with base64. Embedded NUL bytes are a protocol error and must be rejected before conversion to C strings or any storage mutation, never silently truncated. Setting a value to an empty string deletes the key in the selected namespace, subject to the same access checks as a write. Deleting a missing key succeeds. value_stored confirms durable deletion.
Exactly one value_stored or value_failed responds to this request unless the connection closes or a protocol error occurs. Success means the update or deletion has been committed durably, not merely queued for writing.

arg.name: value
arg.summary: NUL-free value, or empty to delete

c2s.name: get_value
c2s.description: Get a value from the kv store, using the same key and namespace rules as set_value. Exactly one value_obtained or value_failed follows unless the connection closes or a protocol error occurs.

c2s.name: request_store_status
c2s.description: Request the current store status. A ready store responds with store_available. No response is emitted while the store is initializing. This request is explicitly allowed before store_available. Completion can be synchronized with a hyprwire roundtrip; completing initialization still emits store_available.

s2c.name: store_available
s2c.description:
This event is sent when the storage backend is initialized and ready. Sending get_value or set_value before receiving store_available results in a store_unavailable protocol error. request_store_status is allowed during initialization.
If the store is already ready, this event is sent immediately upon binding the protocol. Readiness requires no password, display, or user interaction. If initialization fails, the provider must close the connection rather than leave the client waiting indefinitely.
If this event has not arrived after a roundtrip following binding or a status request, initialization was pending when that roundtrip was processed. This is not a guarantee that it will remain pending.
Once available, the store remains available for this connection's lifetime. To withdraw the store, the provider must close existing connections before withdrawing availability. Clients must reconnect and wait for a new store_available event; no availability state survives disconnection.

s2c.name: value_obtained
s2c.description: Response from the kv_store with the NUL-free value.

s2c.name: value_failed
s2c.description: Completes the pending get_value or set_value for this (key, type) pair with an error. value_missing applies only to reads. An I/O error does not promise that a partially completed write was rolled back; only value_stored confirms durability. No successful result follows for the same request.

s2c.name: value_stored
s2c.description: Completes the pending set_value for this (key, type) pair after the update or deletion is durably committed. A transport roundtrip alone is not a write acknowledgement.
